item.title: PVE installed on top of an SDN VXLAN zone: terminal/Web UI stalls and "failed to set mtu to 1500"
item.author: invalid@example.com (Fearless-Grape5584)
item.dc:creator: Fearless-Grape5584
item.content:encoded:
Posting this because I could not find the same case anywhere on the forum or via search, and the symptoms are easy to misread as something else.

TL;DR — If you run a PVE instance whose uplink sits on a network with an MTU below 1500 (an SDN VXLAN vnet gives you 1450), you have to set the MTU manually on both the NIC and the bridge. Setting it on only one of them fixes only half of the symptoms.

item.title: Proxmox Virtual Environment now available for 64-bit ARM (arm64)!
item.author: invalid@example.com (t.lamprecht)
item.dc:creator: t.lamprecht
item.content:encoded:
We are excited to announce the first release of Proxmox Virtual Environment with official support for a second CPU architecture: 64-bit ARM (arm64/aarch64). Until now, Proxmox VE was available for x86-64 (amd64) only.

item.content:encoded:
We recently uploaded the 7.0 (rc6) kernel to our repositories. The current default kernel for the Proxmox VE 9 series is still 6.17, but 7.0 is now an option.

We plan to use the 7.0 kernel as the new default for the upcoming Proxmox VE 9.2 and Proxmox Backup Server 4.2 releases planned later in Q2.
